subject: Inference runway: hosted vs dedicated decision
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@launchpad.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Inference deployment evaluation — latency/throughput details

Olga / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — that was helpful. To make the decision internally we need a short written recap of what we discussed around deployment mode. High level constraints:
- Core customer-facing path needs P95 end-to-end < 150ms (ideally ~100ms) for our recommendation engine.
- Peak qps for the recommendation endpoint is ~450 sustained during campaign windows, with short bursts up to ~900 requests/minute.
- Average token size: ~120 input, ~85 generated.
- Data residency: US-only; some requests contain user identifiers and must not leave our VPC for regulated flows.

We discussed three options (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC). From the call I heard Redwood thinks Dedicated gives most predictable latency for our QPS profile but we want to understand tradeoffs: expected P95 on Dedicated vs Hosted, fallback behaviors, and estimated monthly cost for a pilot.

Can you send a concise recommendation and a proposed next step (pilot or benchmark) plus any artifacts you need from us? Also attach the QPS profile CSV you referenced.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of ML Platform
LaunchPad.ai
From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@launchpad.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inference deployment evaluation — latency/throughput details

Liam — nice to meet you over the call. Recap + recommended next steps below. Attaching the blank QPS template we discussed (please fill with weekday/weekend breakdowns and burst windows).

Short recommendation (summary):
- Pilot on Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for the recommendation endpoint. Reason: Dedicated gives deterministic scheduling and KV cache locality that reduces token-level variance; for your 450 sustained / 900 burst profile we expect more consistent P95s compared to multi-tenant Hosted under similar cost envelope.
- Add a Hosted overflow route as a low-cost burst buffer to handle rare overloaded minutes. Redwood can route overflow automatically to the hosted fleet with rate limits and cost caps.

Expected performance (ballpark):
- Dedicated (n1-ish GPU pool, 16GB model working set): P50 ~ 40–60ms, P95 ~ 90–160ms depending on sequence lengths and batching.
- Hosted overflow: P95 varies more (120–300ms) but useful for short bursts where latency flexibility is acceptable.

Proposed pilot: 2-week Dedicated pilot (thin reservation) to run a true workload benchmark with your traffic pattern + fallback routing enabled. Deliverables: latency/throughput dashboard, token-level cost breakdown, and a short ops runbook.

Action items from LaunchPad: please return the attached CSV with QPS profile + sample anonymized request (no PII) so we can size kernels and batching. Also confirm whether regulated flows must be entirely on your VPC or if we can tokenize/mask before sending to Hosted.

I will loop in Ben and Marissa to prepare a pilot MOU and cost estimate.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: launchpad_qps_profile.csv (blank template)
From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:48:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Inference deployment evaluation — recommended pilot plan (internal)

Ben / Marissa — internal coordination notes from the LaunchPad thread. TL;DR: recommend a 2-week dedicated pilot with hosted overflow. LaunchPad is sensitive to price but needs deterministic P95 ~100–150ms for core flows. They also flagged data residency for regulated requests (US-only).

Proposed internal plan:
1) Size pilot: start with 2 x rtxA5000-style nodes (config TBD) with continuous batching and KV cache enabled; reserve minimal headroom to reproduce burst windows.
2) Run 48h synthetic + 48h shadowed production traffic to validate P95 and cost per token.
3) Deliverable: dashboard, cost breakdown (tokens, infra), runbook with fallback routing configured.
4) Commercial: two-week pilot MOU with a capped usage fee + optional conversion credit if they move to annual Dedicated.

Immediate asks for procurement/SalesOps: draft MOU + estimate, brief note for infra to reserve pilot capacity for week of Dec 14th. I will attach a draft MOU and a one-pager price estimate once you sign off.

Notes: if they insist on VPC-only for regulated flows we may still run the main pilot on Dedicated in Redwood-dedicated tenancy but will need to scope Private deployment (longer lead time and higher fixed cost). Call out as a risk but proceed with pilot to show latency profile.

— Olga
From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@launchpad.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-14T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Inference runway: proposed pilot & next steps

Hi Liam — following internal alignment we have a concrete pilot proposal and next steps. Attaching the pilot MOU draft for your review. Key points below.

Proposal: 2-week Dedicated pilot + Hosted overflow
- Objective: measure P95 and cost under your real traffic profile and validate routing/fallback behavior.
- Capacity: 2 dedicated GPU nodes (config: 2x A5000-equivalent); autoscaling disabled for the pilot to get deterministic metrics.
- Routing: primary to Dedicated pool, auto-overflow to Hosted with a soft cap to avoid cost surprises.
- Outcome: end-of-pilot report with P50/P95/P99, token-level cost, and recommendation for production path (Dedicated vs Private).

Commercials & timeline:
- Pilot fee (capped): see attached MOU draft (pilot_MOU_draft_OLGA_V1.pdf). If LaunchPad converts to an annual Dedicated contract within 30 days we will apply a credit equal to the pilot fee.
- Proposed pilot window: week of Jan 4th (reserve requested from infra now).

Next steps (what we need from you):
1) Confirm you approve the pilot scope and timeline.
2) Send completed QPS CSV + a small sample of anonymized payloads for kernel sizing.
3) Provide procurement contact for an MOU signature (we can do DocuSign).
4) If regulated flows require VPC-only routing, flag them now so we can scope Private deployment in parallel (longer lead time).

We will kick off a short technical checklist call once we have the QPS CSV — 30 minutes to confirm endpoints, sampling, and measurement windows.

Links: HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/LP-2026-038 | MOU draft: https://docsend.com/d/LP-pilot-MOU-2026

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the MOU or sizing.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
